observed_title: An elementary proof of linear programming optimality conditions without using Farkas’ lemma
version: Local PDF: arXiv:1407.1240v1 overlay dated July 4, 2014; title page internal date February 13, 2018. Both observed dates retained; no inferred publication version.

read_ranges.scope: Complete paper.md, title/abstract, Sections 1–10 and all references. Initial output middle clipping was explicitly reread as lines207–390 and391–557. No appendix in this14-page PDF. Original PDF pages8–10 and13 rendered to inspect matrices, perturbation, Figure1 and Farkas bounded auxiliary LP.

topic_relevance.B01: direct: finite-dimensional mixed-form LP multiplier certificates and an elementary Farkas proof.
topic_relevance.B04: adjacent: active-set rank, degeneracy and perturbation; does not prove general conic constraint qualifications or minimax.

definitions.name: Mixed LP and sign convention
definitions.statement: min cᵀx, A_E x=b_E, A_I x≥b_I; A_E full row rank m_E, A=[A_E;A_I]. Equality multipliers unrestricted; inequality multipliers nonnegative in Aᵀλ=c.

definitions.name: Feasible direction
definitions.statement: p≠0 and a positive step interval preserving all constraints; equivalently A_Ep=0 and active inequality rows times p≥0. Inactive rows only bound step length.

definitions.name: Vertex and working set
definitions.statement: Vertex means full column rank n of the active-row matrix; working set contains all independent equality rows and an independent subset of active inequalities. An optimal working set additionally solves Wᵀλ_W=c with its inequality components nonnegative.

theorem_cards.label: Propositions3.1–3.3: weak duality and complementarity
assumptions: Finite real matrices, primal feasibility A_Ex=b_E and A_Ix≥b_I.
Multiplier Aᵀλ=c and λ_I≥0; equality multipliers have no sign condition.
theorem_cards.statement: cᵀx−λᵀb=λ_Iᵀ(A_Ix−b_I)≥0; if complementarity is zero then x is globally optimal with value λᵀb. If λ already certifies the optimal value, every primal optimum is complementary with that same λ.
proof_steps: 作者证明：expand Aᵀλ=c and split equality and inequality slacks, lines191–205,220.
本次核验：the gap identity is exact finite algebra; it proves a sufficient certificate without any rank or Slater condition.
gaps: This gives sufficiency and weak duality; existence of a qualifying multiplier is a separate necessity result.

theorem_cards.label: Lemma4.4: optimal vertex or recession descent
assumptions: Paper’s background convention c≠0,A≠0 and independent equality rows.
theorem_cards.statement: Either cᵀx is bounded below and an optimal vertex exists, or there is p with A_Ep=0,A_Ip≥0,cᵀp<0 giving unbounded descent.
proof_steps: 作者证明：start at any feasible x, find a nonzero null direction of active rows, choose a nonincreasing sign and take the maximal feasible step; newly active row is independent, so active rank increases. If no blocker exists in the descent sign, it is a recession direction. Enumerate the finite vertex set and choose smallest objective, lines287–328.
本次核验：positive finite blocker steps preserve old active rows and strictly increase rank; a recession direction plus any original feasible point gives cᵀ(x+tp)→−∞.
gaps: Original line321 says no more than n executions of Step1. If initial active rank r=0, n rank increases need n+1 Step1 visits including terminal visit. Local correction: at most n−r increases and n−r+1 Step1 checks. This is an iteration-count off-by-one, not a failure of the dichotomy.
Without rank(A)=n the feasible set can have lineality and no vertex, e.g. min x₁+x₂ subject x₁+x₂≥1; multiplier sufficiency still holds.

theorem_cards.label: Propositions5.1 and6.3: degenerate multiplier existence
assumptions: Consistent mixed LP, independent equality rows.
For6.3: rank(A)=n and original objective bounded below.
For5.1: candidate is a nondegenerate vertex, so active matrix is square nonsingular.
theorem_cards.statement: At a nondegenerate vertex, its unique active-row multiplier certifies optimality iff its inequality components are nonnegative. For a bounded-below full-column-rank mixed LP, an optimal vertex and an optimal nonsingular working set exist, and extending working multipliers by zeros gives Aᵀλ=c,λ_I≥0 and complementarity.
proof_steps: 作者证明：negative active inequality multiplier yields feasible descent p=W⁻¹e_i; nonnegative multipliers certify via3.2 (lines340–354).

作者证明：relax each inequality rhs by distinct ε,ε²,…,ε^{m_I}; additional active dependent row would impose a nonzero polynomial equation with a unique ε^j term. Choose sufficiently small ε avoiding its roots, solve perturbed nondegenerate optimum, remove rhs perturbation, and extend multipliers by zero (lines431–521).

本次局部论证补足：perturbed and original LP have identical recession inequalities; if perturbed objective were unbounded, Lemma4.4 gives a direction that also makes the nonempty original LP unbounded. Thus boundedness transfers.

本次局部论证补足：there are finitely many nonsingular choices W and extra rows j, so finitely many nonzero polynomials and positive roots; a common small ε avoids all roots. To justify fixing W as ε varies in Part2, take an ε_k↓0 subsequence with one constant W, which exists by finiteness. Feasible x_{ε_k}=W⁻¹(b_W−e_W(ε_k))→x*=W⁻¹b_W preserves all original inequalities and fixes λ_W=W^{-T}c. This makes explicit the omitted dependence management.
gaps: The paper writes W_ε,q as ε-dependent objects while arguing with a fixed polynomial; its finite-working-set repair is elementary but must be stated separately rather than called a printed hypothesis.
Any working set at a degenerate optimal vertex need not have nonnegative multipliers; existence of one optimal set is the conclusion.
No explicit numeric ε threshold, bit-complexity or solver runtime is given; Figure1 deliberately uses ε=1/2 only as illustration.

theorem_cards.label: Propositions7.1 and8.1: all optima and optimal working sets
assumptions: Consistent LP, rank(A)=n, objective bounded below.
For8.1 the given optimum is a vertex.
theorem_cards.statement: A point is optimal iff feasible and admits Aᵀλ=c,λ_I≥0,λᵀ(Ax−b)=0; the same optimal multiplier works at all optima. Every optimal vertex has a nonsingular optimal working set, possibly different from another optimal vertex’s set.
proof_steps: 作者证明：6.3 supplies an optimal multiplier and3.3 gives complementarity at every other optimum. Keep equality rows and rows with positive multipliers, which must be active at every optimum; complete these independent rows to rank n using the given vertex’s other active rows.
本次核验：a zero multiplier permits the corresponding inequality to become inactive at another optimum, so working-set identity is not invariant.
gaps: The statement on vertices requires full active rank; a general nonvertex optimum may have a smaller independent working set.

theorem_cards.label: Lemma9.1: Farkas alternative with no rank restriction
assumptions: Finite real m×n A and n-vector c; no rank condition on A.
proof_steps: 作者证明：simultaneous feasibility contradicts cᵀp=yᵀAp≥0. Minimize cᵀp subject Ap≥0 and−1≤p_i≤1. The added ±I makes rank n, zero is feasible and the cube is bounded. Optimal multiplier identity c=Aᵀλ₁+λ₂−λ₃ and value cᵀp*=−1ᵀ(λ₂+λ₃) imply zero value⇒λ₂=λ₃=0 and y=λ₁; negative value supplies p.

本次核验：rank assumption is discharged by the bounded auxiliary cube; it is not inherited as a restriction on the original Farkas matrix. Zero c directly gives y=0 and excludes strict-negative p; zero A handled directly if needed rather than invoked under paper’s A≠0 background.
gaps: The proof is for finitely many coordinates and constraints; no infinite-index or infinite-dimensional extension follows.

constant_dependence.explicit: No quantitative error rate. Finite vertex enumeration count ≤binom(m,n) (equality-containing subsets reduce it). Active-rank procedure ≤n−r rank increases; at most n−r+1 Step1 checks. Perturbation exponents1,…,m_I and common ε threshold depend on all nonsingular row subsets and polynomial positive roots; paper gives no explicit threshold or conditioning bound.
constant_dependence.dependence: Multiplier magnitude depends on inverse working matrices W^{-T}; there is no uniform margin or dimension-free certificate conditioning.

endpoint_limits: Rank(A)<n invalidates vertex-existence assertion but not exact multiplier sufficiency.
Degenerate optimum need not certify with every independent active subset.
Strict descent cᵀp<0 distinguishes the Farkas alternative; nonpositive direction is insufficient.
Zero objective/vector/matrix cases should be checked directly under the author’s nonzero background convention.
reusable_methods: Keep mixed inequality direction AIx≥bI and dual signs together.
Audit primal feasibility, stationarity and complementarity as an exact finite certificate before invoking existence theorems.
Use finite working-set enumeration or ε→0 fixed-basis subsequences to justify perturbation arguments.
For Farkas, bound homogeneous directions in a cube, derive a full-rank LP multiplier, then eliminate artificial box multipliers when the optimum is zero.
unchecked: This is full-paper reading with key finite algebra independently checked; it is not certification of all cited books/articles.
No simplex/interior-point implementation run; source educational proof gives no practical complexity theorem.
No transfer to general conic, nonlinear, noncompact infinite LP or center-cube common-input model is asserted.
